'''Thomas Mason''' (born August 9, 1964) is a Canadian-American<ref name=ornl>{{cite web |title=Thom Mason Named Director of Oak Ridge National Laboratory |url=https://www.ornl.gov/news/thom-mason-named-director-oak-ridge-national-laboratory |website=www.ornl.gov |language=en}}</ref> [[condensed-matter physics|condensed-matter physicist]] who serves as the director of [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]]. Prior to this appointment, he had been an executive at [[Battelle Memorial Institute]] from 2017 to 2018, and the director of [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]] from 2007 to 2017.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cho|first1=Adrian |title=Thom Mason, director of Oak Ridge National Laboratory, to step down |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/thom-mason-director-oak-ridge-national-laboratory-step-down |accessdate=2 December 2018 |work=Science   |date=27 February 2017 |language=en}}</ref>  Mason moved to Oak Ridge in 1998 at the start of construction of the [[Spallation Neutron Source]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://neutrons.ornl.gov/sns|title = Spallation Neutron Source &#124; Neutron Science at ORNL}}</ref> which he led from 2001 until project completion in 2006.

== Early life ==
Mason was born in [[Dartmouth, Nova Scotia]], in [[Halifax, Nova Scotia]], [[Canada]].<ref name=ornl /> His father was a [[geophysicist]] who worked at the [[Bedford Institute of Oceanography]], and his mother a [[biochemist]], was working at [[Dalhousie University]] in Halifax.<ref>{{Cite web|date=April 19, 2018|title=Thomas Mason's Interview {{!}} Manhattan Project Voices|url=https://www.manhattanprojectvoices.org/oral-histories/thomas-masons-interview|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210118004241/https://www.manhattanprojectvoices.org/oral-histories/thomas-masons-interview|archive-date=January 18, 2021|access-date=February 2, 2022|website=Voices of the Manhattan Project}}</ref>

In 1986, Mason received his Bachelor in Science from Dalhousie University. In 1990, Mason received his doctorate in physics from [[McMaster University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ORCID |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1880-3971 |access-date=2022-05-04 |website=orcid.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Mason |first=Thomas E. |date=2014-06-18 |title=MacSphere: Critical Behavior of CsMnBr 3 |url=https://macsphere.mcmaster.ca/handle/11375/8328 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220113213503/https://macsphere.mcmaster.ca/handle/11375/8328 |archive-date=2022-01-13 |website=MacSphere: McMaster University Libraries Institutional Repository|type=thesis }}</ref> In 1997, Mason was listed on [[Maclean's]] 100 Canadians To Watch list for his work in [[neutron scattering]] research. At the time, he was an associate professor in physics at the [[University of Toronto]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=To Light The Darkness {{!}} Maclean's {{!}} JULY 1, 1997 |url=https://archive.macleans.ca/article/1997/07/01/to-light-the-darkness |access-date=2022-05-04 |website=Maclean's {{!}} The Complete Archive |language=en-US}}{{dead link|date=October 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

==Career==
Mason started his career in the United States as the science director of the Spallation Neutron Source project in 1998. In 2007, Mason became the director of [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]], succeeding Dr. Jeffrey Wadsworth as the lab's 14th director.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ORNL Directors {{!}} ORNL |url=https://www.ornl.gov/content/ornl-directors |access-date=2022-05-04 |website=www.ornl.gov}}</ref> He stepped down from the position in 2017 to serve as the senior vice president for laboratory operations at [[Battelle Memorial Institute]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Thom Mason, director of Oak Ridge National Laboratory, to step down |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/thom-mason-director-oak-ridge-national-laboratory-step-down |access-date=2022-05-04 |website=www.science.org |language=en}}</ref>

Mason became director at Los Alamos as part of the new Triad National Security LLC management team. In June, 2018, the [[National Nuclear Security Administration]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.energy.gov/nnsa/nuclear-security|title=Nuclear Security|website=Energy.gov}}</ref> headed by [[Lisa Gordon-Hagerty]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.energy.gov/nnsa/contributors/lisa-e-gordon-hagerty|title=Lisa E. Gordon-Hagerty}}</ref> announced that it had awarded an agency, called Triad National Security LLC,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://triadns.org/|title=TRIAD National Security|first=Ann|last=Rafferty|website=TRIAD National Security, LLC}}</ref>  the $25 billion contract for security of the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]]. Triad replaced the former [[Los Alamos National Security]]. The announcement of this action occurred on June 8, with notice to proceed on July 5, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local_news/triad-takes-over-at-los-alamos-on-nov-1-names-mason-director-designate/article_8fe64fcd-85c5-597f-9677-af8486a4ac46.html|title=Triad takes over at Los Alamos on Nov. 1, names Mason director designate|first=Rebecca|last= Moss|website=Santa Fe New Mexican|date=9 July 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independentnews.com/news/new-senior-managers-named-at-los-alamos/article_277e1bca-853c-11e8-878e-6f9a1f7143b8.html|title=New Senior Managers Named at Los Alamos|website=The Independent|date=12 May 2023 }}</ref><ref>[https://www.battelle.org/newsroom/press-releases/press-releases-detail/battelle-and-triad-team-partners-awarded-new-contract-to-manage-and-operate-los-alamos-national-laboratory Battelle and Triad Team Partners Awarded New Contract to Manage and Operate Los Alamos National Laboratory]</ref> The contract includes a five-year base with five one-year options, for a total of 10 years if all options are exercised. With this contract came the appointment of Mason on November 1, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lanl.gov/about/leadership-governance/director.php|title=Laboratory Director|first=Los Alamos National Laboratory, Operated by Los Alamos National Security, LLC, for the U. S. Department of|last=Energy|website=www.lanl.gov}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.manhattanprojectvoices.org/oral-histories/thomas-masons-interview|title=Thomas Mason's Interview|website=www.manhattanprojectvoices.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://triadns.org/leadership-team/|title=Leadership Team|first=Ann|last=Rafferty}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.exchangemonitor.com/dont-screw-interview-incoming-los-alamos-lab-director-thomas-mason/|title='Don't Screw Up': An Interview With Incoming Los Alamos Lab Director Thomas Mason|date=July 27, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/news/article/A-M-chancellor-announces-director-for-Los-Alamos-13085477.php|title=Texas A&M chancellor announces director for Los Alamos lab|first=Victoria|last=Cheyne|date=July 19, 2018|website=Houston Chronicle}}</ref>

In December 2022, the operating and management contract for Triad National Security LLC was extended from Nov. 1, 2023 through Oct. 30, 2028.<ref>{{Cite news |last=O'Neill |first=Maire |date=December 7, 2022 |title=Mason Says Triad LLC Five-Year Contract Extension Is Direct Result of Workforce's Hard Work and Dedication |url=https://losalamosreporter.com/2022/12/07/mason-says-triad-llc-five-year-contract-extension-is-direct-result-of-workforces-hard-work-and-dedication/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230607151603/https://losalamosreporter.com/2022/12/07/mason-says-triad-llc-five-year-contract-extension-is-direct-result-of-workforces-hard-work-and-dedication/ |archive-date=June 7, 2023 |work=Los Alamos Reporter}}</ref>
